newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse-French vote sends signals on ECB.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse-French vote sends signals on ECB.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Monday that France's swing to the left in Sunday's elections signalled certain dangers for the common currency project.
"The outcome of the parliamentary election in France holds the danger that the independence of the future European central bank might be weakened," Hesse said in a speech.

Hesse who is also the president of the state central bank in Lower Saxony, Saxony Anhalt and Bremen said France's swing to the left could be seen to unleash forces which opposed such a supra-national group of experts.

At the same time he said that the road to Europe's currency union was currently at its most difficult. "He who is legally bound to uphold price stability could no longer support a project where this goal could be seen to be in danger of being diluted," Hesse said, adding however "but I am not giving up yet."

The left-wing victory as well as Germany's unusually public row between the Bundesbank and Bonn over the proceeds of a planned revaluation of reserves have cast dark clouds over the common currency project.
